chunks: Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyib asked ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn عليهما السلام and said to him:
When was the salat (prayer) made obligatory upon the Muslims in the form it is upon today? He said:

In al-Madīnah, when the daʿwah became manifest, Islam grew strong, and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, prescribed jihad upon the Muslims. The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله added seven rakʿahs to the salat (prayer): two in al-Ẓuhr, two in al-ʿAṣr, one in al-Maghrib, and two in al-ʿIshāʾ al-Ākhirah, and he left al-Fajr as it had been prescribed in Makkah, in order to hasten the ascent of the angels of the night to the heaven and to hasten the descent of the angels of the day to the earth. So the angels of the day and the angels of the night would witness Salat al-Fajr with the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله; therefore Allah, Blessed and Exalted, said:
“And the Qur'an of dawn; surely the Qur'an of dawn is witnessed.”
The Muslims witness it, and the angels of the day and the angels of the night witness it.

key_terms.الدَّعْوَةُ: the public manifestation of the call to Islam
key_terms.الصَّلَاةُ: the prescribed salat (prayer) made obligatory upon the Muslims
key_terms.الْجِهَادَ: the divinely prescribed jihad upon the Muslims
key_terms.الْفَجْرِ: the dawn prayer left in its original prescribed form
key_terms.رَكَعَاتٍ: the units of ritual prayer added to the daily salat
key_terms.مَلَائِكَةُ: the angels who witness the dawn prayer

ai.seo_question: When were the daily prayers fixed in their current number of rakʿahs, and why is Fajr especially witnessed?
ai.summary: This hadith explains that the salat (prayer) was established in its present form in al-Madīnah after Islam had become manifest and strengthened. It also links the special status of Salat al-Fajr to the witnessing of both the angels of the night and the angels of the day, illuminating the meaning of the Qur'anic phrase about the dawn recitation being witnessed.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.1319 - Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib asked Ali ibn al-Hussain (as),
"When was the prayer made obligatory upon the Muslims in the form it is today?"

He (as) replied: "In Medina, when the call (to Islam) became manifest, Islam was strengthened, and Allah (swt), the Mighty and Majestic, prescribed jihad upon the Muslims.
The Messenger of Allah (sw) added seven rak'ahs to the prayers: two to Dhuhr, two to Asr, one to Maghrib, and two to the Isha prayer, while leaving the Fajr prayer as it had been prescribed in Mecca.
This was to hasten the ascent of the night’s angels to the heavens and the descent of the day’s angels to the earth. Thus, the angels of the night and the angels of the day would witness the Fajr prayer with the Messenger of Allah (sw).
This is why Allah (swt), Blessed and Exalted, said: 'Recite the Qur'an at dawn. Indeed, the recitation of the Qur'an at dawn is ever witnessed' (Qur'an 17:78)
witnessed by the Muslims and by the angels of the night and the angels of the day."
